Class GameState

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am14.model.gameLogic.GameState
Direct Known Subclasses:
ControlState, EndGameState, EndRoundState, GameStateTest.TestGameState, PickState, PositionState, WaitingRoomAfterCrashState, WaitingRoomState
abstract class GameState extends Object
Abstract base for all game states; implements the State design pattern.

Each concrete subclass represents one logical state of the game (for example: waiting room, position selection, picking, end-of-round, end-of-game, etc.). The Game context delegates state-specific behavior to the current GameState instance: actions such as placeTotem(Game, Player, char), pickCard(Game, Player, Optional, int) and onPlayerConnection(Game, String, String) are handled by the active state object.

This class acts as the engine of the game's state machine: subclasses override the operation methods to provide permitted behavior for that state and implement nextState(Game) to perform state transitions. Default implementations throw WrongStateException (or perform no-op) to enforce that only allowed operations succeed in a given state.

Responsibilities:

  • Define the state interface for game operations.
  • Provide default (disabled) implementations that raise WrongStateException.
  • Require subclasses to implement nextState(Game) to advance the state machine.
  • Serve as the single place to add or modify state-specific logic and transitions.

Note: concrete states may throw or propagate domain-specific exceptions (e.g. IllegalPickException, ForcedPickException, WrongTurnException, UnknownPositionException, IllegalPlacementException) to signal invalid operations according to game rules.

    • controlPick

      protected void controlPick(Game context, boolean addTopPick, Card selectedCard, int row) throws SQLException
      Initiates the control cycle after a card pick to evaluate the validity and consequences of the action.

      By default, this method performs no operation. Concrete subclasses (specifically ControlState) override this method to handle post-pick validations, process additional pick allowances, update turn counters, and compute whether control remains with the current player or transitions.

      Parameters:
      context - the game context in which this action is performed
      addTopPick - true if this step covers an extra top pick; false for regular drafts
      selectedCard - the card involved in the action
      row - the board row index where the selection was performed
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database or state persistence error occurs during state transitions

    • getStateName

      protected String getStateName()
      Retrieves the canonical text identifier associated with this specific game state.

      This identifier is primarily utilized by the client-side architecture (e.g., ClientModel) to recognize, track, or reset the current state representation. By default, this base implementation returns null. Concrete state subclasses are expected to override this method to return their unique string designation (e.g., "PICK", "PLACE").

      Returns:
      a String representing the state mode, or null if not explicitly defined by the subclass
